name: Peregrine Mission One
payload: Peregrine lander, 1,283 kg at launch (Wikipedia); 20 payloads, five of them NASA instruments; never reached the Moon
type: COMMERCIAL LANDER · NEVER REACHED THE MOON
first: Flown on the first Vulcan Centaur; a propellant leak ended the Moon landing before it began
description: Peregrine Mission One was an Astrobotic lunar lander, flown for NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services with 20 payloads, five of them NASA instruments. It launched on 2024-01-08 on the first flight of the Vulcan Centaur and separated from the upper stage at 08:09 UTC. The planned flight was a highly elliptical Earth orbit with its apogee at the Moon's distance, 1.5 loops, then an interception of the Moon. Instead, the oxidiser-tank pressure rose after separation and, 92 minutes later, an oxidiser tank ruptured and the leak spun the lander. Astrobotic's review board found that a helium pressure valve most likely lost its seal. The landing was called off. Peregrine reached the Moon's distance on about 2024-01-12, and on 2024-01-13 Astrobotic and NASA decided to end the mission. Burns of its main engines moved the re-entry over the South Pacific, where it re-entered on 2024-01-18 at about 21:04 UTC, after 10 days 14 hours of flight.

events.label: SEPARATION
events.note: Peregrine separates from the Centaur at 08:09 UTC.

events.label: TANK RUPTURE
events.note: 92 minutes after separation an oxidiser tank ruptures and the leak spins the lander; the landing is called off.

events.label: MOON'S DISTANCE
events.note: About 2024-01-12, about 238,000 miles from Earth, with no Moon to meet.

events.label: MISSION ENDED
events.note: 2024-01-13: Astrobotic and NASA decide to end the mission and aim the re-entry at the South Pacific.
